commons.title: Group of Pārsīwans in 1878-1880.jpg
commons.description: A five-member group of Parsiwans posing for a photo in the courtyard of a government palace (known then as Wali Sher Ali Khan's Zenana) in Kandahar, Afghanistan. The man partially shown standing on the left appears to be a guard, and there's a dog sitting at the top of the steps in the background.
commons.editorial_reason: Caption and source category specifically identify Parsiwans, and the image visibly shows their traditional dress and group setting.

commons.title: Herati Soldiers 1879.jpg
commons.description: Two soldiers from the Afghan Revolt, 1879: a Herati (Tajik) soldier from Herat and a Ghilzai soldier from Kalat-i-Ghilzai. Drawn by Frank Dadd, published in The Illustrated London News (1880). They wear red uniforms with sabres and traditional telpek hats.
commons.editorial_reason: The caption identifies the subjects as a Herati Tajik and a Ghilzai soldier, not specifically Farsiwan; the source category alone conflicts with the caption.
